Governor Okpebholo said insecurity was one of the biggest challenges he met on assumption of office and that he had discussed the security situation and the state of roads in Edo with President Bola Tinubu. He said he responded to the Vegetable Market kidnapping incident by informing the President about the attack and assuring him the state would handle it. The governor said he prayed for the arrest of the perpetrators within 24 hours before instructing the Commissioner of Police. “I told him I wanted these guys arrested because I already have an approval from God, and they were caught within that time,” Okpebholo was quoted as saying on Friday. He began struggling to breathe and used three inhalers he had with him, but they failed to provide relief. item.title: Tomato prices remain high as pepper gets cheaper in Lagos
item.description: The drop in pepper prices has brought some relief to traders and buyers in Lagos markets, but the high cost of tomatoes continues to weigh on traders’ sales and consumers’ purchasing power. Traders and consumers who spoke with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in separate interview in Lagos described how changing prices had affected sales, household spending and the quantities of produce they could afford. They cited seasonal availability and transportation costs among the factors influencing the market. Malam Mohammed, a tomato seller at Costain Bus Stop, said he sourced his produce from Mile 12 Market, where prices varied according to variety, size and place of origin. He said a paint of tomatoes, which sold for N6,000 in August and September, now cost N7,000, while a basket had risen from between N35,000 and N40,000 to between N45,000 and N65,000. Mohammed explained that the high cost of tomatoes made it difficult for traders to maximise profits, adding that some customers complained about the sizes and quantities they received for the prices paid. “This business is not a straight business,” he said. Owho recalled that a basket sold for about N40,000 in August and September, although prices fluctuated during that period. She said the frequent changes made it difficult for traders to predict their purchasing costs, adding that the basket she bought on the day of the interview cost N40,000. Mrs Mary Chigozie, a resident of Vaughan Street, Costain, said she spent between N2,000 and N5,000 daily on tomatoes and pepper but had reduced the quantities used in cooking because of the high cost of tomatoes. She said small quantities of tomatoes that previously sold for N200 or N300 now cost N500 or N1,000. Chigozie explained that she sometimes combined pepper with tomato paste or prepared red-oil stew when fresh tomatoes became too expensive. She expressed concern that prices could rise further during the December festive period and urged the government to support and protect farmers. On pepper, Mrs Rukayat Rasheeb, a trader at Olaogun Street, Abule-Nla Junction, Costain, said a bag currently sold for between N45,000 and N60,000, the same price range recorded in August and September. She, however, observed that pepper was now more plentiful than during the earlier period. Rasheeb explained that prices generally declined when pepper was in season and increased when it became scarce. She expressed optimism that prices could fall further, while noting that transportation and loading expenses added to traders’ costs. Mr Okoro Ebubechi, who also sells pepper at Olaogun Street, Abule-Nla Junction, said he currently bought a small basket for N20,000, compared with between N30,000 and N40,000 in September. He attributed the reduction to increased availability during the current season, adding that transportation expenses influenced the prices charged by traders. Ebubechi said customers were buying larger quantities because pepper had become more affordable. He added that he sold pepper in different quantities, including portions worth N500, to accommodate buyers with varying budgets. He expected prices to rise again in December if pepper became less available. Mrs Odunayo Igwe, a pepper trader at Ilogbo Mosque, Apapa Road, said a bag currently sold for N30,000, the same price recorded in September. She explained that although the price had remained unchanged, pepper was now more plentiful than in September, when supplies were lower. Igwe also identified transportation costs as a factor affecting selling prices and expressed hope that prices would decline further. Mrs Patience Niju, a pepper seller at Suru Market, Suru-Alaba, said she currently bought a small bag for N25,000 and a larger bag for N40,000. She added that a small bag of shombo cost N20,000, while a larger one sold for N30,000. Niju said the prices were unchanged from August and September, but the bags contained more pepper in October. She welcomed the increased quantity, saying it encouraged customers to buy more and helped her sales move faster. Mrs Teni David, a civil servant residing in Iyana Ipaja, said N200 to N500 could now buy more pepper than in August and September, when the same quantity cost between N1,000 and N1,500. She said the increased availability had enabled her to buy larger quantities for household consumption. David attributed the seasonal glut partly to limited preservation facilities, explaining that large quantities of pepper entered the market as the produce ripened, prompting traders to sell quickly before it lost its freshness. She called on the government to establish more processing centres where farmers and traders could preserve and package pepper during periods of abundance. According to her, such facilities would help reduce waste and maintain supplies during the off-season. David warned that prices could rise again when the current season ended. Ms Mary Udonwa, another pepper consumer, said the produce had become more affordable, allowing households to buy larger quantities. She said she currently spent between N500 and N1,500 on pepper, depending on her needs. Udonwa explained that high prices in August and September had forced her to reduce the amount used in cooking, sometimes relying on small quantities or ground pepper when fresh pepper became expensive. She attributed the current reduction to increased market supply and suggested that some sellers might be lowering prices to avoid losses from spoilage. The I-G also said that the committee was made up of representatives of the Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation. item.title: Police arrest suspect over railway vandalism in Ogun, recover 16 iron rods
item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 36-year-old man, Shobande Taofeek, over alleged vandalism and theft of railway infrastructure in the Arigbajo area of the state. The police also recovered 16 railway iron rods and two gas cylinders suspected to have been stolen during the operation. The arrest was carried out by operatives of the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) unit of the command following intelligence reports about the alleged vandalism and theft of railway materials in the area. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Ogun State Command, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, said the operatives intensified surveillance and patrols in the affected area on Friday October 23, leading to the suspect’s arrest. According to the statement, the suspect subsequently led the operatives to an uncompleted building where the recovered items were found. “On 23 October 2026, SWAT operatives intensified surveillance and patrols in the affected area, leading to the suspect’s arrest. He subsequently led the operatives to an uncompleted building where the stolen items were recovered as exhibits,” the statement said. The police further disclosed that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect had allegedly admitted involvement in similar offences on three previous occasions. However, the command said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the alleged crime and identify other individuals who might have been involved. “Efforts are ongoing to apprehend other suspects connected with the crime and recover any additional stolen property,” the statement added. The State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting public assets and critical infrastructure, warning that those responsible for vandalism would be brought to justice. Ojajuni, according to the statement, reaffirmed the command’s “unwavering commitment to protecting public assets, safeguarding critical infrastructure and bringing perpetrators of economic sabotage to justice.” He also called on residents to support security agencies by providing credible and timely information that could help prevent crime and protect public infrastructure across the state. The police urged members of the public to cooperate with law enforcement agencies, stressing the importance of community participation in crime prevention and the maintenance of safer communities. item.title: Real Madrid’s Courtois to miss El Classico due to illness
item.description: Real Madrid have suffered a major setback ahead of their El Clasico clash against Barcelona after goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was ruled out of Sunday’s La Liga encounter due to illness. The Belgian goalkeeper has contracted the flu and will miss the Matchday 10 fixture at Camp Nou, forcing Madrid to turn to Ukrainian shot-stopper Andriy Lunin. The development comes at a crucial time for Real Madrid, who trail Barcelona by six points in the La Liga standings and need a positive result to strengthen their title challenge. Real Madrid confirmed Courtois’ late withdrawal in a statement released hours before kick-off. “Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal from tonight’s LaLiga matchday 10 game between Real Madrid and Barcelona due to a bout of the flu,” the club said. “Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the squad in his place.” Courtois’ absence represents a significant blow for Madrid, given his importance to the team and his recent performances. The 34-year-old was in action during Madrid’s recent Champions League outing, in which the club reportedly secured a 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig. His late withdrawal leaves Lunin with the responsibility of guarding Madrid’s goal in one of the most important fixtures of the season. Lunin is expected to start in goal in place of Courtois as Madrid prepare to face their fierce rivals. The 27-year-old has served as Courtois’ deputy in recent seasons and gained valuable experience during Madrid’s run to the Champions League final in 2024. He will now face a major test against a Barcelona side that has enjoyed an impressive start to the domestic campaign. Barcelona head into the encounter looking to maintain their strong league form, while Madrid will be eager to close the gap at the top of the standings. Madrid’s preparations have been further complicated by the absence of forward Vinícius Júnior, who remains unavailable as he serves a four-match domestic suspension. The Brazilian’s absence deprives Madrid of an important attacking option for the high-profile encounter. Madrid have also suffered two league defeats this season, against Real Betis and Atletico Madrid, increasing the pressure on the team to secure a result against Barcelona. With Courtois ruled out at the last minute and Vinícius unavailable, Madrid face a difficult challenge as they seek to reduce Barcelona’s six-point advantage in the La Liga title race. item.title: Taraba Govt mobilizes emergency relief, food supplies to Binnari after bandit attack
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Taraba State Government has deployed emergency relief materials to Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area, less than 24 hours after a deadly bandit raid left more than forty residents dead and several households displaced. The rapid humanitarian intervention was executed on the direct directive of Governor Agbu Kefas, who mandated immediate state assistance to cushion the hardships faced by survivors of the Friday afternoon incursion. A high-powered government delegation led by the Executive Secretary of the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA), Dr. Audu Echuseh, arrived in the community on Saturday to coordinate the distribution of relief items and assess the extent of property destruction. The assessment team included the members representing Karim Lamido Constituencies at the Taraba State House of Assembly, Hon. Anas Shuaibu Didango and Hon. Abner Shittu; the Vice Chairman of Karim Lamido Local Government Council, Alhaji Uba Munyarda; alongside traditional rulers and community stakeholders. Addressing grieving residents during the distribution of supplies which included food grains, mattresses, blankets, and essential non-food items, Dr. Echuseh conveyed Governor Kefas’s deepest condolences to the bereaved families. She stated: “We are here on behalf of the Taraba State Government to show solidarity and provide immediate succour to our brothers and sisters in Binnari. His Excellency has directed that no victim of this dastardly act be left unattended to. “This is just the first phase of our intervention. The government is fully committed to providing necessary humanitarian support while collaborating with security agencies to ensure long-term stability and security in the area.” Reacting to the prompt response, the lawmakers commended the state government for its swift action, pledging total grassroots cooperation with security formations deployed to comb the area and forestall future attacks. Although the police claimed ten persons were killed, residents of the community said more than forty residents were lost to the attack. item.title: ‘My daughter, my biggest priority’ – Naomi Osaka considers quitting tennis
item.description: Former world number one Naomi Osaka cast doubt on her future Sunday saying she would consider quitting tennis if her three-year-old daughter asked her to. The four-time Grand Slam champion from Japan took 15 months away from the sport after the birth of her daughter Shai, before returning in 2023. She is in Tokyo to play at the Pan Pacific Open this week and said becoming a mother had reshaped her priorities. “I wouldn’t say I’m part-timing it but my entire day doesn’t consist of that,” said the 29-year-old, now ranked 19 in the world. “It’s tough, sometimes I look towards my future and I often wonder how long I’m going to play. “Because if my daughter did say she didn’t want me to travel as much, I’m not the type of person to ignore that.” Osaka also stepped away from tennis in 2021 to prioritise her mental health. She said her “mindset is changing a lot” with age. “My daughter is my biggest priority,” she said. “I try my best to put as much energy as I can into tennis. “If I think about it in certain ways, I’m really proud of where I am now because it’s not like I can dedicate my entire time to the sport.” – Online abuse – Osaka said juggling her duties as a player and a mother was something she was “figuring out little by little”. She also offered support to the American Coco Gauff, who said she had received an “insane” amount of racist abuse on the internet at this month’s China Open. World number five Gauff, who is Black, said the experience had been “kind of draining”. Osaka, whose mother is Japanese and father from Haiti, said “nobody should have to go through that”. “It’s sad but I’m used to it on my end,” she said. “I feel like for me, I’ve dealt with that my entire career through decisions that I make that seem to make some people upset. It’s tough.” Osaka said efforts made by women’s tennis governing body the WTA to combat social media abuse did not “ever seem to fully work all the way”. “I know that some people are like, OK, if it bothers you that much, stay off social media,” said Osaka. “But sometimes that’s the best way to connect with your fans. “From my end, what I do about it is I don’t really go on social media at all.” Osaka is seeded seven in Tokyo and plays Italy’s Jasmine Paolini in the first round. World number one Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan and Philippines sensation Alexandra Eala are also competing. Osaka said she was “not far off” refinding her best form and was “optimistic for next year”. item.title: 2027: Tinubu has lost touch with reality, unaware he’s president — Shaibu
item.description: The Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, has accused President Bola Tinubu of losing touch with reality, alleging that he is disconnected from the economic hardship facing Nigerians. Shaibu made the allegation during an interview on ARISE News on Sunday, faulting the president for blaming the opposition for hunger despite spending three and a half years in office. “He has lost touch with reality. Bola is not aware of his environment. He is not aware of what Nigerians are going through. He’s not even aware that he’s president,” Shaibu said. He described Tinubu’s explanation of the country’s hunger crisis as delusional, arguing that the president should take responsibility for the economic situation under his administration. “I watched him yesterday and my eight-year-old son who was beside me said, what’s this man talking about? He has been in office for three and a half years. And he’s talking about hunger being created by the opposition. I think it is delusional,” he said. Shaibu challenged Tinubu to compare the cost of living when he assumed office on May 29, 2023, with the current situation, arguing that Nigerians should not be worse off under his leadership. He cited the removal of petrol subsidy as a major factor behind rising prices, saying the policy triggered sharp increases in the cost of goods and services. “Bola Tinubu claimed the podium, and announced that subsidy was gone. And boom, what happened? Everything rose astronomically. The Nigerians cannot afford three square meals today,” he said. The ADC campaign official also alleged that higher university fees had forced some students out of school, despite the establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). He further criticised Tinubu for continuing to blame the opposition, noting that the All Progressives Congress governed the country for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari before handing over power in 2023. Shaibu said Tinubu’s remarks on hunger raised questions about his understanding of the hardship experienced by ordinary Nigerians. He argued that the president should be held accountable for his administration’s economic policies rather than attributing the crisis to political opponents. item.title: 2027: Engaging APC data boys, insult to my integrity — Pat Utomi
item.description: A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Professor Pat Utomi, has described engaging social media users he accused of being All Progressives Congress (APC) supporters paid to troll critics as an insult to his integrity. Utomi said the users began attacking him after he raised concerns about the living and working conditions of Nigerian soldiers, whom he said were poorly paid despite risking their lives to protect the country. In a post on X on Sunday, the economist alleged that some of those who criticised him were APC supporters benefiting from what he described as “stomach infrastructure”. “Yesterday, we talked about the poor living and working conditions of Nigerian soldiers compared to their counterparts in the US, and how senators are fattening their pockets with billions of naira while the soldiers who risk their lives every day to protect us are underpaid heavily,” he wrote. He said some social media users attacked him after he raised the issue, prompting him to examine their profiles. “Then, some fellows benefiting from stomach infrastructure began to bash us. I took a quick look at their profiles, and it became obvious to me that they were APC data boys trolling anyone who dared to speak up,” Utomi said. He added that he would not engage with the accounts, saying, “Engaging with any of them is an insult to my integrity.” In a separate post, Utomi also accused APC politicians of attempting to intimidate Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. He said Nigerians should not allow such actions to discourage them from participating in the electoral process. “We have seen videos of APC politicians trying to intimidate Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he wrote. Utomi urged Nigerians to unite and resist what he described as attempts to instil fear ahead of the polls. “Nigerians need to understand that these fellows are powerless when we stand united. Do not allow them to sow seeds of fear in you,” he said. He also called on voters to participate in the election and protect the integrity of their votes. “Come out, vote, and defend your votes,” Utomi added. item.title: 1,314 protesters arrested in France over unrest
item.description: Police arrested 1,314 people in weekend protests across France, the interior ministry said Sunday, adding that 53 officers were hurt in clashes. The arrests occurred as violence broke out on the margins of mass demonstrations in major cities on Saturday over the high cost of living. It was the second consecutive weekend of unrest in France, which is heading to presidential elections in April and May to choose a successor to Emmanuel Macron, who is reaching his two-term limit. The interior ministry said police responded to 75 fires during Saturday’s protests, adding that 24 shops were looted. “Several investigations have been opened,” it said in a statement, without giving details. It said that the rest of Saturday night, after the clashes had died down, was “calm”. The ministry statement on Sunday did not say how many protesters were hurt. Late Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez spoke of two serious injuries among protesters: one in Toulouse and one in Clermont-Ferrand. – Protesters hurt – The Toulouse prefecture, which reports to the interior ministry, told AFP that a 20-year-old man was seriously hurt with a wound to his hand. A street medic who tended demonstrators told AFP, on condition of anonymity, that the man had “several fingers” blown off his right hand. The prefecture covering Clermont-Ferrand said a man there also had a hand hurt, but did not suffer the loss of any fingers. A French regional daily, La Nouvelle Republique, reported that a man in Poitiers was hurt in his left eye, showing a photo of a man holding his face. The newspaper’s photographer told AFP he was a 19-year-old who was wounded during a charge by riot police firing stun grenades and tear gas. There have been several instances in recent weeks, during student protests in France, of people being maimed by police stun grenades or tear gas grenades. It was not known if the injuries reported from Saturday were from those police weapons. item.title: Mother, child die as two container trucks overturn in Lagos
item.description: By Efe Onodjae A mother and her child have died after two heavily laden 20-foot container trucks overturned at Mile 2, near Freeman Market, inward Apapa, Lagos. The victims were trapped beneath the overturned trucks and their containers during the incident, which occurred over the weekend. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, said its rescue and recovery personnel responded to the scene to evacuate the victims and remove the wreckage. According to the agency, the road was temporarily cordoned off, while traffic was diverted through an adjoining service lane to ease congestion and prevent further accidents. LASTMA deployed a crane and a high-capacity tow vehicle to remove the overturned trucks and their cargoes, while officers of the Nigeria Police Force provided security during the operation. The remains of the victims were subsequently conveyed to the police mortuary in Yaba for necessary procedures. The General Manager of LASTMA, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed sadness over the incident and called for a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident. He urged relevant security agencies to determine whether mechanical defects, excessive loading, improper cargo distribution, driver negligence or other factors contributed to the incident. Bakare-Oki also called on truck operators to ensure their vehicles were roadworthy, secure their cargoes properly and comply with established road safety regulations. item.title: NDLEA arrests US-based grandma, South African woman with large cocaine, loud shipments
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) disclosed on Sunday that it’s operatives have arrested a 62-year-old Nigerian-American grandmother, Anetor Gloria Ubong, with 9.45kg of high-grade cannabis, loud, imported from the United States and a 34-year-old South African woman, Qhina Beauty, with 36.65 kilograms of cocaine at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos. The agency added that in separate operations across the country, NDLEA officers also recovered tons of illicit drugs in Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta states. Spokesman of the agency, Femi Babafemi said, “Qhina, the South African, was arrested at the departure hall of the Lagos airport on 7th October 2026 while trying to board a Qatar Airways flight to South Africa via Doha. “A search of her two travelling bags led to the recovery of 30 blocks of cocaine weighing 36.65kg, laced with dried pepper, wrapped in cello tape and packed into seven separate parcels. “During her interview, she told operatives she arrived in Nigeria on 30th September specifically to pick up the consignment. She said she was recruited by another South African lady, who promised her R20,000 on successful delivery. “She claimed she was introduced to two other members of the syndicate: one based in the United States and the other a Lagos-based car dealer. “Investigations later led to the arrest, on 14th October, of the 46-year-old car dealer Uchenna Victor Umunnakwe, who was intercepted at Apple Junction, Ago Palace Way, Lagos, after days of surveillance at his Shasha residence. “He admitted receiving Qhina at the airport, lodging her at Santiago Hotel in Amuwo-Odofin, and later moving her to Cynarisso Hotel near the airport, ahead of her departure. “In another interdiction operation at the Lagos airport, NDLEA officers on Wednesday, 21st October, arrested a 62-year-old grandma Anetor Gloria Ubong, a realtor based in Richmond, Texas, who holds both Nigerian and US passports. “She was arrested following her arrival on a United Airlines flight from Houston. Spokesman of the agency, Femi Babafemi said, “Qhina, the South African, was arrested at the departure hall of the Lagos airport on 7th October 2026 while trying to board a Qatar Airways flight to South Africa via Doha. “A search of her two travelling bags led to the recovery of 30 blocks of cocaine weighing 36.65kg, laced with dried pepper, wrapped in cello tape and packed into seven separate parcels. “During her interview, she told operatives she arrived in Nigeria on 30th September specifically to pick up the consignment. She said she was recruited by another South African lady, who promised her R20,000 on successful delivery. “She claimed she was introduced to two other members of the syndicate: one based in the United States and the other a Lagos-based car dealer. “Investigations later led to the arrest, on 14th October, of the 46-year-old car dealer Uchenna Victor Umunnakwe, who was intercepted at Apple Junction, Ago Palace Way, Lagos, after days of surveillance at his Shasha residence. “He admitted receiving Qhina at the airport, lodging her at Santiago Hotel in Amuwo-Odofin, and later moving her to Cynarisso Hotel near the airport, ahead of her departure. “In another interdiction operation at the Lagos airport, NDLEA officers on Wednesday, 21st October, arrested a 62-year-old grandma Anetor Gloria Ubong, a realtor based in Richmond, Texas, who holds both Nigerian and US passports. “She was arrested following her arrival on a United Airlines flight from Houston. A search of her two checked-in boxes uncovered 18 parcels of loud, a synthetic cannabis weighing 9.45kg, concealed with gift wrapping paper in a box. “She claimed the box was delivered to her home in the US by her daughter and the daughter’s future brother-in-law, for onward delivery in Nigeria to her daughter’s fiancé, Jibola. Meanwhile, operatives of a special operations unit in NDLEA on Friday, 23rd October arrested Eletu Rasheedat, 41, at Eti Osa in area of Lagos where they recovered 5,820 pills of diazepam, 780 tablets of tramadol, 3.7kg skunk and 230.25 litres of skuchies. In Delta, a suspect Peter Ugochukwu, 51, was arrested in Warri with a huge cache of pharmaceutical opioids including 29,350 capsules of tramadol; 6,620 tablets of tramadol 200mg; 4,116 bottles of codeine syrup; 11,340 tablets of Rohypnol; 3,500 tablets of diazepam; 300 ampoules of pentazocine injection, 200 ampoules of diazepam injection, and quantities of tramadol 225mg, Molly and Cocodamol. He was transferred along with a white Hummer bus from the Nigeria Police Force, Delta State. In a separate arrest at Enhere Junction, Warri, a 46-year-old physically challenged woman, Helen Bakporo Samson, was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Monday 19th October with 6.0kg of skunk. A 41-year-old suspect Fajana Dada Oluwaseyi, was arrested on Monday 19th October in Adamasingba, Ibadan, following his initial escape from arrest when NDLEA officers seized 197.8kg of cannabis sativa from his house on 16th September. The agency said a raid in Gerawa area of Kano on Thursday 22nd October led to the arrest of Murtala Lawan, 30, and seizure of 159 blocks of cannabis sativa weighing 97.2kg, NDLEA officers at the Lankaviri checkpoint, Yorro LGA, Taraba on Friday 23rd October arrested Raiyanu Misa, 39, with 95 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 60.175kg. The same day, the Nigeria Police Force handed over a suspect arrested at Dakka village, Bali LGA, with 112 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 81.49kg. In Niger state, Emmanuel Ekene, 26, was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Monday 19th October on the Sabo-Kainji road, Borgu LGA, with 64,000 pills of opioids including tramadol and diazepam, while officers arrested Jamilu Mustapha, (aka Last Card), 45, on Wednesday 21st October at Nasaru Town, Ningi LGA, Bauchi state where they seized 379kg of cannabis sativa packed in seven jumbo sacks. Acting on intelligence, NDLEA officers on Tuesday 20th October raided a farm at Board-Ala, Akure South, Ondo state and recovered 56 bags of abandoned cannabis sativa weighing 583kg. Two cannabis farms in Ugbada Forest, Uzebba, Owan West LGA, Edo state, with an estimated yield of 2,023.14kg, were destroyed on Sunday 18th October by NDLEA operatives who also burnt 450kg of processed cannabis at the site and took 97kg as exhibit. In a related operation at Ewe community, Owan West, Mary Edokhai, 42, was arrested with 35kg of same psychoactive substance. With the same vigour, Commands and formations of the Agency across the country continued their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitization activities to schools, worship centres, work places and communities among others in the past week. These include: WADA enlightenment lecture to students and staff of Oje Grammar School, Ibadan, Oyo state; Government Day Secondary School, Kwamba, Niger state; Baptist Primary School, Olorunda, Ogun state; Government Secondary School, Yalea, Kano; Community Secondary School, Igogoro, Enugu; Urban Girls Secondary School, Onitsha, Anambra; and Kelebe Community Grammar School, Osogbo, Osun state, among others. While commending the officers and men of MMIA, Kano, Lagos, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta Commands for their vigilance, diligence, professionalism and intelligence-driven approach to the various successful operations, Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (rtd) urged them and their colleagues across the country to sustain the tempo of the war against drug trafficking and substance abuse. item.title: Troops neutralise 6 terrorists, arrest 11 suspected collaborators in Borno
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised six terrorists, arrested 11 suspected collaborators and received the surrender of a Jama’atu Ahlis Sunna Lidda’awati wal-Jihad (JAS) member in Borno. This is contained in an operational report made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), on Sunday in Abuja. The report said the operations, conducted by troops of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), targeted terrorist fighters and suspected support networks in Kaga and Gwoza Local Government Areas. It said troops of 29 Task Force Brigade Garrison, supported by Hybrid Force personnel, ambushed suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP)/JAS terrorists along the Targejeri axis of Kaga at about 12:37 a.m. on Oct. 25. According to the report, six terrorists were neutralised during the encounter, while troops recovered an AK-47 rifle, three magazines and 169 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. “Other recovered items included two Android phones, three button phones and charms. “In a related development, troops arrested six additional suspected terrorist collaborators during a follow-up raid in Benisheikh, Kaga, at about 6:20 a.m. on Oct. 24. “The arrests brought the number of suspects apprehended in connection with the investigation to 11, including five earlier arrests. “Items listed as recovered during the raid included an AK-47 rifle, three empty magazines, 169 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three terrorist uniforms, a turban, a head mask, two Android phones, three button phones and charms,” it said. The report said the suspects were undergoing investigation to establish their alleged involvement in terrorist activities and identify possible links to other members of the network. It added that troops of 192 Battalion (Main), supported by Hybrid Force personnel at Hambagda Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) Camp in Gwoza, received a JAS member who surrendered at about 9:20 p.m. on Saturday. According to the report, preliminary investigation indicated that the individual had escaped from a terrorist enclave in the Mandara Mountains area of Gwoza and decided to abandon terrorism. “The individual surrendered with an AK-47 rifle and a magazine containing 28 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition,” it added. The report said the defector was in custody undergoing further investigation and processing in line with established procedures. It said the operations underscore OPHK’s continued efforts to disrupt terrorist activities, dismantle support networks and encourage defections through sustained, intelligence-led operations. The military urged members of the public to provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore peace and enable displaced communities to return safely. item.description: Sekinat Osundiji A polling unit is where voters go to cast their ballots during an election. It is also where election officials verify voters’ identities, issue ballot papers, and count votes after voting ends. For many Nigerians, understanding what happens at a polling unit can help them prepare for election day and know what to expect when they arrive to vote. Here is how the process works. Voters arrive at their polling units On election day, registered voters go to the polling units where their names appear on the voters’ register. They are expected to check their polling unit before leaving home to avoid going to the wrong location. At the polling unit, officials organise voters and direct them to the appropriate queues. Security personnel may also be present to maintain order and prevent disruptions. Election officials verify voters Before voting, officials check the voters’ register to confirm that each person is registered at that polling unit. The voter’s identity is then verified using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), which is used by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for voter accreditation. The system checks the voter’s details and may use fingerprint or facial recognition, depending on the circumstances. If accreditation is unsuccessful, officials follow INEC’s prescribed procedures. Only voters who meet the accreditation requirements are allowed to proceed to vote. Depending on the election, voters may receive separate ballot papers for positions such as president, governor, senator or member of the House of Representatives. The counting process is expected to be transparent, allowing those present to observe and raise concerns through the proper channels. Results are announced at the polling unit After counting, the presiding officer records the results on the prescribed result sheet. The results are announced at the polling unit, and party agents and other authorised persons can observe the process. Where applicable, the results are uploaded electronically through INEC’s designated result-transmission system. The polling-unit result is then taken through the appropriate collation process, where results from different polling units are combined at higher levels. The result announced at one polling unit does not, by itself, determine the overall winner of the election. What can voters do if something goes wrong? Voters who experience problems, including difficulties with accreditation, disputes over voting procedures or suspected irregularities, can raise their concerns with the presiding officer. They can also report incidents to authorised election officials or security personnel where appropriate. Party agents and accredited observers may document incidents and report them through the relevant channels. Voters should avoid violence, intimidation or actions that could disrupt the process. Election complaints should be handled through the procedures established by INEC and the relevant legal authorities. Why the polling unit matters The polling unit is the starting point of the election results process. Every valid vote recorded there contributes to the results that are collated across the country. Understanding the process helps voters know their rights, follow the correct procedures and recognise when something may be wrong. For voters, election day is not simply about arriving at a polling unit and choosing a candidate. It also involves accreditation, ballot secrecy, transparent counting and the proper recording of results. Each stage plays a role in ensuring that the votes cast are properly accounted for. AFP journalists saw police charge several times and vigorously use tear gas and batons against some, mostly young, protesters. Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February. Protests have also been taking place in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems.
